Chapter.Heading: Introduction
Chapter.Section:
GAP Jupyter Kernel
This package provides a so-called kernel for the https://jupyter.org interactive document system.
This kernel is implemented in &GAP;.

Installation
The supported frontend environment is &Jupyter; Notebook 7 or JupyterLab 4, with Python 3.8 or later, on Linux or macOS. Classic Notebook 5 and 6 are not supported. Further instructions for installing &Jupyter; can be found at https://jupyter.org/install. This package requires the &GAP; packages &IO;, &uuid;, &ZeroMQInterface;, &crypting;, and &json;, all of which are distributed with &GAP;, and some of which require compilation. To compile &ZeroMQInterface; you need to install &ZeroMQ;, for details please refer to the https://gap-packages.github.io/ZeroMQInterface/doc/chap0.html.
&JupyterKernel; itself does not contain any kernel code that needs to be compiled.
It is necessary to register &JupyterKernel; with your &Jupyter; installation.
Installing the kernel and its prebuilt JupyterLab extension from the package directory works as follows:
> pip install .
or registering for your user only
> pip install . --user
This installs the Python launcher, the gap-4 kernel specification, and the jupyterlab-gap-mode syntax-highlighting extension. End users who install a wheel do not need Node.js; building from a source checkout requires Node.js 18 or later.
If &GAP; is not in your PATH, set the environment variable JUPYTER_GAP_EXECUTABLE to the absolute path of the &GAP; executable.
To start &Jupyter; run:
> jupyter notebook
or:
> jupyter lab
Then &JupyterKernel; should show up in your &Jupyter; installation as "GAP 4".
JupyterHub does not require a separate integration. Install the wheel in the Python environment used by jupyterhub-singleuser, or in a shared &Jupyter; prefix visible to the single-user environments. Each single-user server must be able to find &GAP; through PATH or JUPYTER_GAP_EXECUTABLE.
Support on Windows is experimental. The kernel protocol, interrupts, and demo notebook execution are tested with both Python and &GAP; inside Cygwin. The full JupyterLab / &Jupyter; Server stack is not currently supported in Cygwin, so this is not yet an end-user JupyterLab installation path for Windows.

Section.Heading: How it works
Section.Subsection:
Kernel Startup
This section gives a short explanation how the process of executing &GAP; as a kernel by &Jupyter; works to help with debugging issues.
&Jupyter; registers kernels using json files in various directories. You can list which kernel specifications are installed by executing the following command
> jupyter kernelspec list Available kernels: python3 /usr/local/share/jupyter/kernels/python3 gap-4 /usr/local/share/jupyter/kernels/gap-4
If there is no line containing the gap-4 kernel, something went wrong with the Python package installation. Report the issue on the issue tracker, giving which operating system you are using, your versions of &Jupyter; and &GAP;, and which installation commands you ran.
When &Jupyter; starts a &GAP; kernel, the kernel specification invokes python -m gap_jupyter_kernel. This launcher finds &GAP;, replaces itself with the &GAP; process, loads this package, and runs the kernel.

Kernel operation
The communication between the &Jupyter; frontend and &GAP; happens through ZeroMQ streams as documented https://jupyter-client.readthedocs.io/en/latest/messaging.html, encoded as JSON dicts.
After entering code into a cell and instructing &Jupyter; to execute that code, the jupyter frontend sends the code to the &GAP; session where it is executed by using the &GAP; function READ_ALL_COMMANDS, resulting values of the execution are rendered using ViewString and sent back to the &Jupyter; frontend.
In principle, rich rendering of content, as exemplified in the function JUPYTER_DotSplash is possible.
Tab-completion is handled by the &GAP; function JUPYTER_completion, and inspection is handled by JUPYTER_Inspect.
Changing these functions, one can change the behaviour of Tab-completion and inspection to improve user experience.

Chapter.Section:
Code Highlighting and Indentation
&JupyterKernel; provides a CodeMirror 6 &GAP; mode with syntax highlighting. It is installed as the prebuilt jupyterlab-gap-mode extension and registers text/x-gap as a MIME type in JupyterLab 4 and Notebook 7.

Known Limitations and Caveats
Currently the support of the &GAP; system for alternative frontends is a work in progress. In particular, certain outputs that are printed by &GAP; cannot be captured by the &Jupyter; frontend and will not show up.
On Windows, only the experimental Cygwin kernel path described above is tested; the full JupyterLab / &Jupyter; Server stack is not supported.

The variables last, last2 and last3 (see ) are also unsupported in the current version.
If you happen to notice problems of this kind, feel free to report them on the https://github.com/gap-packages/JupyterKernel/issues. or suggest a solution via a pull-request.
